activities.activityType: Guided concept learning with unaided changed problem
activities.instructions:
Part A - concepts (about 20 min): Read/write the relation V = I × R and rearrange it as I = V / R and R = V / I. In a series circuit state: the same current flows through every component; the supply voltage divides across components; total resistance is the sum of the individual resistances. Work one worked example given as: supply 12 V, R1 = 200 Ω, R2 = 400 Ω. Compute R_total = 200 + 400 = 600 Ω, I = 12/600 = 0.02 A, V1 = 0.02×200 = 4 V, V2 = 0.02×400 = 8 V, and check 4 + 8 = 12 V.
Part B - unaided changed circuit (about 20-30 min), do this without looking back at Part A: supply 9 V with R1 = 100 Ω and R2 = 200 Ω. (1) Find R_total. (2) Find the current I. (3) Find the voltage across each resistor. (4) Verify the two voltage drops add to the supply voltage. (5) In your own words explain why the current is the same through both resistors and how you found total resistance.
Part C - check (about 10 min): Compare each of your five answers against your own recomputation; correct any arithmetic slip, then state your final answers and explanation aloud or in writing. Stop when Part B is correct and explained; do not repeat further circuits.
